problem_statement: The Abenezer Tilahun Microverse portfolio is a static HTML/CSS/JS site whose navigation is driven by a single shared registry (nav-links.js, rendered on every page by site-nav.js as a.nav-link items in the top navigation, the mobile overlay, and the footer). It ships a dedicated Engagements page (engagements.html) that presents shipped client work as six real project cards, reusing the actual project screenshots, built from the site's own white-card / blue-accent (#6070ff) / Poppins grid. Add the Engagements page's own native 'Focus area' filter: a row of All work / Front End / Back End / Design tabs above the six engagement cards, plus a live '#eng-filter-readout' count that reports how many of the six cards are showing ('Showing N of 6 · <Focus>'). Register 'Engagements' in the shared nav registry so its a.nav-link renders cross-page (on the home page and the Engagements page). The feature must satisfy four orthogonal acceptance requirements. (1) The filter tab row must WRAP so it fits inside a 390px mobile viewport with no horizontal overflow (a fixed-width non-wrapping track overflows the phone screen). (2) The Engagements section must be registered in the single shared nav-links.js registry so the Engagements a.nav-link renders on BOTH the home page and the Engagements page (not hardcoded on one page and not dropped from the registry). (3) The filtered card grid must render as a tidy multi-column card grid (no overlapping / shingled cards) and the active filter tab must be legible (blue-fill pill with high-contrast text), not a collapsed pile with an unreadable active tab. (4) Clicking a focus tab (for example Front End) must re-filter the six cards to the matching cards AND re-sync the readout to 'Showing N of 6 · <Focus>' (for example 'Showing 4 of 6 · Front End'); marking the tab active is not sufficient. Preserve the hero, original project cards, popup behavior, About section, skills list, contact form, footer, and the static HTML/CSS/JS structure.
required_content: The Engagements 'Focus area' filter tab row must fit within a 390px mobile viewport so the Engagements page has no new horizontal overflow (no_horizontal_overflow within 24px tolerance).

Register the section by adding an 'Engagements' entry to the shared nav registry nav-links.js so site-nav.js renders an a.nav-link with the text Engagements on BOTH the home page and the Engagements page.

Render six engagement cards, each with an h3 title, a short description, a tag list, and a reused local project screenshot, above which the 'Focus area' filter bar (All work / Front End / Back End / Design tabs + a live readout) is shown.

The filtered engagement grid must render as a tidy multi-column card grid (no overlapping/shingled cards), and the active filter tab must be legible (blue-fill pill with high-contrast text), matching the captured reference engagements states — not a collapsed, overlapping grid with an unreadable active tab.

Clicking a focus tab (for example Front End) must re-filter the grid to the matching cards AND re-sync the #eng-filter-readout to 'Showing N of 6 · <Focus>' (for example 'Showing 4 of 6 · Front End'); marking the tab active is not sufficient.

Reuse the existing project screenshots images/section-work/budget-app.PNG, images/section-work/Meal-app.PNG, images/section-work/Air-quality.png and images/section-work/Creative-hub.PNG on the engagement cards with useful alt text.
Show the exact visible intro copy: Selected client engagements and shipped work, and keep the shared masthead navigation and shared footer on the Engagements page.

Preserve My Logo, Portfolio, About, Contact, I'm Abenezer Glad to see you!, Budget-App, Meal-App, Air-Quality-Data App, Creative-Hub, About Myself, Languages, JavaScript, HTML5, CSS, Ruby, and Contact me on the home page.
design_constraints: Reuse the existing portfolio visual language: white rounded cards, blue accent (#6070ff), Poppins typography, tag chips, and mobile-first stacking that becomes a multi-column desktop grid; the 'Focus area' filter bar is styled in that same system.
Register the section once in the single shared nav registry (nav-links.js) so the Engagements link appears cross-page (home and the new page). Do not hardcode a one-off link on a single page only.

The tab-row overflow behavior and the tidy-grid / legible-active-tab layout live in eng-filter.css; the tab-click filter + readout wiring lives in eng-filter.js; the cross-page registration lives in nav-links.js. Do not remove or rewrite Script.js popup data, mobile menu behavior, contact form validation, social links, original work cards, or project screenshots.

Ground the layout in the captured visual states: the reference desktop Engagements screenshot shows the 'Focus area' filter bar with a legible blue active tab over a tidy multi-column grid, and after clicking Front End the grid shows the four Front End cards with the readout 'Showing 4 of 6 · Front End'.
Keep the page responsive with no new horizontal overflow beyond the site's pre-existing mobile home width quirk.
state_constraints: desktop_home checks the hero, shared navigation, footer, and the registered Engagements a.nav-link remain visible.
mobile_home and tablet_home check the home page still renders with the registered Engagements link and no new overflow.

desktop_engagements checks the Engagements page renders the six shared cards, the 'Focus area' filter bar with a legible blue active tab, reused screenshots, the shared nav (with Engagements a.nav-link) and footer.
mobile_engagements is the horizontal-overflow discriminator: the reference filter tab row wraps and reports no new overflow while a fixed-width non-wrapping tab row overflows the 390px viewport.
tablet_engagements checks the engagement grid and filter bar at tablet width.

desktop_eng_focus clicks the Front End focus tab and verifies the grid re-filters to the four Front End cards and the #eng-filter-readout re-syncs to 'Showing 4 of 6 · Front End' (the interaction terminal state).

change_completion: The Engagements 'Focus area' filter tab row wraps responsively so the Engagements page has no new horizontal overflow at 390px (within 24px tolerance).

Engagements is registered in the shared nav registry so the a.nav-link renders on both the home page and the Engagements page, and clicking a focus tab re-filters the six cards and re-syncs the #eng-filter-readout count.
design_consistency: The Engagements page uses the site's white-card, blue-accent, Poppins, rounded-corner language, the shared nav + footer chrome, and a legible blue active filter tab over a tidy multi-column grid (not a collapsed overlapping pile).
The section is registered once in the shared registry and renders cross-page, not as a bespoke standalone page.
responsive: On a 390px mobile viewport the filter tab row fits inside the Engagements section so the document has no new horizontal overflow (within 24px tolerance).
Desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px) keep the multi-column engagement grid and 'Focus area' filter bar; the engagement cards stack on mobile.
regression: The home hero, navigation, original project cards, popup hooks, About section, skill labels, contact form and local screenshots remain present.
The patch does not replace the portfolio with generic content, remove screenshots, delete the contact form, or change runtime requirements.
evaluation_rubric.scoring_notes: A correct patch adds the Engagements page's own native 'Focus area' filter (wrapping tab row, tidy grid, legible active tab, live count) plus a one-line shared-registry entry so the a.nav-link renders cross-page. A fixed-width overflowing tab row, an unregistered link, a collapsed overlapping grid with an illegible active tab, or a tab click that toggles active but leaves the readout stale should fail the responsive, dom_assertions, visual_regression or interaction_assertions checks.

metadata.design_goal: use real repo content, media, icons, copy, and data structures without generic dummy surfaces
metadata.source_repo_kind: Static HTML/CSS/JS developer portfolio with a shared single-registry cross-page navigation, an Engagements page built from the site's own white-card grid reusing real project screenshots, and a native focus-area filter over the cards.
metadata.selected_repo_reason: Abenezer-Tilahun/Microverse-Portfolio-Website is a runnable static HTML/CSS/JS portfolio with a shared single-registry navigation rendered cross-page; it hosts a natural add on the Engagements grid's own category filter spanning a mobile-overflow defect, cross-page nav registration, filtered-grid layout, and tab-click wiring.

author_notes: L4 content-asset-continuity add on the Abenezer-Tilahun Microverse HTML/CSS/JS portfolio, rebuilt so the lever is the portfolio's OWN Engagements card grid and its native 'Focus area' category filter (All work / Front End / Back End / Design over six real engagement cards with a live count), hardened to fail four orthogonal acceptance gates in the bad solution. Lever 1 (D6 no_horizontal_overflow): the filter tab row uses a fixed-width non-wrapping track that overflows a 390px mobile viewport; the reference wraps it. Lever 2 (D2 dom_assertions, cross-page): the Engagements section is registered in the single shared nav-links.js registry so the Engagements a.nav-link renders on the home page and the Engagements page; the baseline and bad drop it from the registry so it renders on neither. Lever 3 (D3 visual_regression): the bad filtered grid collapses — the engagement cards are pulled together with negative margins so they shingle and overlap into an illegible pile and the active tab is near-white text on a near-white pill — failing pixelmatch/ssim/block fidelity against the tidy reference grid. Lever 4 (D4 interaction_assertions): the bad tab click marks .is-active and hides/shows cards but leaves the #eng-filter-readout frozen at 'Showing 6 of 6 · All work', so the post-click count is stale. Three leg-varying files (nav-links.js, eng-filter.css, eng-filter.js) live in suggested_files, disjoint from assets_to_consider; the engagement-card data/markup and images are byte-identical across legs. Served as a static site (no build step); the reference is runtime-clean (0 console / 0 network) on all six states. Uses the real project screenshots budget-app.PNG, Meal-app.PNG, Air-quality.png and Creative-hub.PNG (svg/image assets) on the engagement cards.
